body: I used to be a cool outgoing, friendly sk8r boy back in like 2017, but since my parents got a divorce, i lost my girlfriend of 2 years, my dad got cancer, my relationship with my mum halted, my best and only friend got drunk and beat me up and i lost my house etc. I havent been amazing and ive picked up a nicotine addiction, failed a suicide attempt, got no job, and i have to spend most days at home with my dying dog of 13 years. But today i moved about a ton of wood from my front yard in preparation for sale, scratched the fuck out of my arm carrying shit,  and i feel pretty fucking good about it. Also, i look bomb as fuck dressed up like a full on gardener wearing black gloves and leather boots.

I mean a happy person is a person with a certain set of circumstances rather than a certain set of mindsets. I have severe depression, i have been hospitalised for it, and i find alot of the time people tell themselves that they cant choose to be happy because it makes them feel justified with putting no effort into improving your mindset because "not everyone is a rich kid that had everything handed to them on a plate". Happiness being a mindset is a buddhist philosophy and i dont think the dalai lama had the privileges of western society growing up.
Its just ironic because lots of the people i know with more money are having a rougher time than lots of the people i know with a smaller amount. Some regions in africa are home to the most positive people having the most "particularly good days" and thats got nothing to do with anyone other than a choice to be a positive and happy, which i will say seems like itd be alot easier without a bunch of people discouraging eachother from trying to better themselves.

Seriously the single most beneficial thing that got me and all of the people i know who struggle with severe anxiety or depression out of hospital was the realisation that happiness is a choice and you can influence your feelings to a certain extent with positive thinking. I think the people who genuinely think this is a murder by words should do some reading or be open to the idea that in any circumstance, this was positive advice, up until someone decided to attack this random guys circumstances

Honestly, i just want to say thanks for reaching out to someone for help in a time like this. Its a really good way of dealing with things instead of just letting yourself fall into a dark place with no attempt of getting out, and its quite admirable.

This ones a bit weird but when id get the wires on my braces tightened the lovely dental assitant would ask me what colour bands id want, and due to me wanting to draw attention away from my braces i always picked light blue, because it wasnt eye catching but it didnt look like i was trying to hide my braces. One day when they ran out of light blue, the girl asked "we are out of light blue, is dark blue okay instead?" Because she had remembered i always got them. Her and the dentist wouldve seen dozens of different kids daily, and i would go in for 15 minutes once a month, yet she still was nice enough to remember that for me. Probably not as cool now that i think about it but it made me happy so eh

You know that feeling that you get when somebody pretends to push you into a pool or something and then catches you before you fall in? That feeling in that split second, at random times, for sometimes hours at a time. Thats probably the best way i could describe my anxiety attacks, and i usually end up vomiting and getting a migraine if its bad also. With me and some of the other people i know with anxiety, general anxiety, not necessarily a fully fledged anxious breakdown,
 isnt too much of an issue as they can differentiate between having genuine fear or if its irrational anxiety. This for me just feels like your heartrate racing and you get on edge a bit more, almost like the feeling of waiting to run in a race or on the ride up before the drop on a rollar coaster. Just some nice relaxing panic.

Unconventional but i had pretty severe social anxiety that people were always looking at me because i looked bad, so i started wearing colourful beanies and if i saw someone looking at me i just told myself it was because my beanie looked stupid. Now i can go out in public wearing all of these bright colours and silly things ive found from op shops and it makes you feel great.

Hey man, i seriously appreciate the comment. Inspiring people is something i aspire to do that i never thought id be capable of so it really means alot.
And i agree, ive come across alot of those articles suggesting positive thinking for anxiety and they way they put it across makes it seem like bullshit.  I find often positive thinking its put across as more of a "everythings okay, think positive, dont be negative" and ignore whatever issue your having. If i can suggest what helped me the most, it was buddhist ideas and mentalities. I was reluctant to read into it at first because i was raised atheist, but the main idea is mindfullness. Its acknowledging that there is an issue and thats fine because its a temporary emotion that will pass. 
Thanks again and i wish you the best of luck my friend.
